entities.name: Konrad VIII the Younger
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Konrad VIII the Younger, a scion of the Silesian Piast dynasty, held ducal authority over various territories within the fragmented Duchy of Oleśnica (Oels) in Silesia during the tumultuous early to mid-15th century. Born into a cadet branch of the Piasts, he jointly ruled Oleśnica, Koźle, and parts of Bytom and Ścinawa from 1416 to 1427, before consolidating sole control over half of Ścinawa until his death on September 5, 1444. His reign, though localized, unfolded amidst the volatile backdrop of the Hussite Wars, a period that dramatically reshaped the political and religious landscape of Central Europe, forcing Silesian principalities to navigate complex allegiances between the Holy Roman Empire, Bohemia, and the burgeoning Hussite movement.

The ducal succession in Oleśnica was characterized by a system of fraternal co-rule, and Konrad VIII initially shared power with his brothers, Konrad V Kantner, Konrad VI the Elder, Konrad VII the White, and Konrad IX the Black. This collective governance of the Oleśnica lands, including the strategically important Koźle and fragmented Bytom, reflects the common practice of dividing patrimonial inheritances among male heirs in medieval Central Europe. His participation in the anti-Hussite crusades, particularly during the early 1420s, aligned him with the Catholic forces attempting to suppress the Bohemian reformers. These military engagements often resulted in devastating raids on Silesian territories by Hussite armies, impacting his ducal domains directly and contributing to the economic instability of the region.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Konrad VIII played a notable role in the complex political landscape of 15th-century Silesia, navigating the Hussite Wars and contributing to the defense of Catholic interests in the region. His reign exemplifies the challenges faced by minor Central European rulers during a period of intense religious and territorial upheaval.
